title: UT Health East Texas Expands Access to Care with New Facility in Whitehouse
summary: UT Health East Texas Expands Access to Care with New Facility in Whitehouse wroberts Mon, 08/31/2026 - 12:04 WHITEHOUSE, Texas (Aug. 25, 2026) — UT Health East Texas is expanding access to high-quality healthcare with a new, state-of-the-art facility that is under construction in Whitehouse. The more than 11,000-square-foot clinic, located on Highway 110, is designed to meet the growing needs of families in southern Smith County. “This location is situated along a growth corridor in southeastern Smith County,” said Steven Cox, MD, UT Tyler School of Medicine Faculty Practice Plan President. “As our community expands, we remain committed to meeting the increasing demand for quality healthcare close to home. This investment ensures that families in this area have convenient access to the care they need, when they need it.” Located at 710 Highway 110 N., next to the Taco Bell, the facility will house six family medicine providers and feature on-site X-ray and laboratory services, offering patients a convenient, one-stop destination for comprehensive care. “Our goal is to make healthcare more accessible and convenient for the communities we serve,” said Jason Boyd, chief operating officer of UT Health East Texas Physicians. “By bringing multiple services under one roof, we’re able to streamline the patient experience and deliver timely, coordinated care closer to home.” In addition to treating illness and providing preventive annual wellness visits, providers at the clinic will offer a range of services, including joint injections and minor procedures such as stitches and wart removal. Walk-in appointments will also be accommodated as availability allows. “Primary care is the foundation of a healthier community,” said Dr. Michael Racs, DO, MBA, primary care medical director of UT Health East Texas Physicians. “This new clinic allows us to expand access to preventive care, chronic disease management and same-day medical needs for patients in Whitehouse and the surrounding communities. By bringing more providers and services to this area, we can help patients build lasting relationships with their care teams and receive the right care at the right time.” About UT Health East Texas UT Health East Texas provides care to thousands of patients each year through an extensive regional network that includes nine hospitals, more than 90 clinics, the Olympic Plaza Tower, 13 regional rehabilitation facilities, two freestanding emergency centers, regional home health services, an EMS fleet of more than 65 ambulances and four helicopters, and a comprehensive eight-trauma center care network, including the region's only Level 1 trauma facility. As a partner with The University of Texas System, UT Health East Texas is uniquely positioned to provide patients with access to leading-edge research and clinical therapies while training and educating the next generation of physicians and other health professionals.
body_markdown:
**WHITEHOUSE, Texas (Aug. 25, 2026)** —[UT Health East Texas](https://uthealtheasttexas.com/) is expanding access to high-quality healthcare with a new, state-of-the-art facility that is under construction in Whitehouse. The more than 11,000-square-foot clinic, located on Highway 110, is designed to meet the growing needs of families in southern Smith County.


“This location is situated along a growth corridor in southeastern Smith County,” said Steven Cox, MD, UT Tyler School of Medicine Faculty Practice Plan President. “As our community expands, we remain committed to meeting the increasing demand for quality healthcare close to home. This investment ensures that families in this area have convenient access to the care they need, when they need it.”


Located at 710 Highway 110 N., next to the Taco Bell, the facility will house six family medicine providers and feature on-site X-ray and laboratory services, offering patients a convenient, one-stop destination for comprehensive care.


“Our goal is to make healthcare more accessible and convenient for the communities we serve,” said Jason Boyd, chief operating officer of UT Health East Texas Physicians. “By bringing multiple services under one roof, we’re able to streamline the patient experience and deliver timely, coordinated care closer to home.”


In addition to treating illness and providing preventive annual wellness visits, providers at the clinic will offer a range of services, including joint injections and minor procedures such as stitches and wart removal. Walk-in appointments will also be accommodated as availability allows.


“Primary care is the foundation of a healthier community,” said Dr. Michael Racs, DO, MBA, primary care medical director of UT Health East Texas Physicians. “This new clinic allows us to expand access to preventive care, chronic disease management and same-day medical needs for patients in Whitehouse and the surrounding communities. By bringing more providers and services to this area, we can help patients build lasting relationships with their care teams and receive the right care at the right time.”


**About UT Health East Texas**
UT Health East Texas provides care to thousands of patients each year through an extensive regional network that includes nine hospitals, more than 90 clinics, the Olympic Plaza Tower, 13 regional rehabilitation facilities, two freestanding emergency centers, regional home health services, an EMS fleet of more than 65 ambulances and four helicopters, and a comprehensive eight-trauma center care network, including the region's only Level 1 trauma facility. As a partner with The University of Texas System, UT Health East Texas is uniquely positioned to provide patients with access to leading-edge research and clinical therapies while training and educating the next generation of physicians and other health professionals.
